title: Are You Cyclone Ready?
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: NDIS , Western Australia , Cyclone , Emergency , Pilbara , Embrace , Karratha Are You Cyclone Ready? A cyclone warning has just been put in place for our area, and it’s time to dust off your supplies and get prepared for the next few days. You may be aware of what you need in your basic kit, such as a torch, water and fresh batteries. You probably know to fill your car with petrol, to tape down your windows and to bring in any furniture from outside the home. If you’re looking for a quick reminder and a basic cyclone-ready checklist, click here. But for someone with a disability, things can be a bit more tricky around cyclone season. You may have special needs that won’t be found on any official checklist, such as an extra supply of catheters, or a plan for evacuating using a wheelchair. You may be feeling anxious about how you’ll cope if a cyclone hits, or be worried if you’ll be able to contact people in an emergency. Some good planning and some extra stockpiling could make all the difference to your health and wellbeing, if a cyclone does hit. Here at Embrace we support all our clients to be prepared for natural disasters, including cyclones. We are creating a planning tool to help you choose what suits you best, and can be tailored to your

title: Are You Cyclone Ready?
text: unique needs and abilities. As soon as our planning tool is up and functional, we’ll let you know. But for now, read on to get cyclone ready. The New Cyclone Warning System You’re probably aware that the WA government has changed their cyclone warning system. Gone are the colour-coded alerts: they’ve been replaced with “Advice”, “Watch and Act” and “Emergency Warning”. Part of being cyclone-ready is knowing what these three new levels mean, and how they impact you. As a basic guide, “Advice” is about listening out for information about a cyclone that is forecast, and preparing things like your emergency kit; “Watch and Act” is for putting your cyclone plan into place because the cyclone is coming soon; and the “Emergency Warning” is for when the cyclone has hit and you need to take shelter. For more info on the new alert system, visit https://www.dfes.wa.gov.au/hazard-information/cyclone/prepare?tab=local Before the cyclone Before the cyclone hits is your time to prepare all those last-minute things on your list, such as double-checking your kit, getting online to the Emergency WA website , bringing any pets inside, and making sure you have some cash in your wallet. Now is also the time to be preparing for any special needs you may have, such as requiring electricity to run a vital piece of equipment, or having enough food for a guide dog, or making sure you have enough medicine or pharmacy supplies like incontinence pads. It’s a great time to go over your personalised checklist and

title: Are You Cyclone Ready?
text: tick off each item. This will help you feel prepared physically as well as mentally and emotionally. If you have been told to evacuate, this is time to use your checklist to grab everything you will need to stay a few nights in a shelter. You may need to stay in emergency accommodation for several weeks afterwards, so you’ll need to pack for this too. If you are evacuating, there’s some things you won’t need to take, such as drinking water, but you’ll need to make room in your bag for any items which won’t be readily available in a typical shelter, such as your ventilator or strapping for a limb. If you know the cyclone is just about to hit, now is the time to turn off the electricity mains, gas and water if you’ve been advised to. During the cyclone Once the Emergency WA website has issued a red “Emergency Warning” it will be too late to leave your home. You will need to choose the strongest part of your house to stay in, so keeping away from doors and windows is advised. Have your emergency kit close by, including any medicines and generators you may need. It’s now time to break out your stash of treats (we love chocolate here at Embrace!), turn the radio on if you can, and be patient while the storm passes. You may hear a lot of howling noises, and might witness glass shattering or other loud, dangerous things happening. There will

title: Are You Cyclone Ready?
text: be a lot of rain, wind and clattering sounds that you might not have heard before. If loud noises affect you, now is the time to put some earplugs in or some noise-canceling headphones on. Many cyclone survivors report that the howling noise of the wind made them feel extra anxious, so try to remember that these noises are a normal part of the cyclone and that they will pass eventually. After the cyclone Once you start to hear more rain than wind again, you’re most likely on the other side of cyclone, so now is a good time to check in with the radio and/or the Emergency WA website to track how the cyclone is moving. Do not open any doors until you know it is safe to do so. The website will outline what damage has occurred outside, and whether you need to take extra precautions when leaving your home. It could still be dangerous outside with things such as powerlines down, trees fallen or flooding occurring, so you really must check with official sources before leaving your home. If you’re wheelchair bound or find walking challenging, it might still be dangerous to leave the home, even after it has been deemed “safe” to go outside: the ground may be uneven, or your usual routes may be closed. It’s best to call someone to double check your area for you, and if you have trouble getting a friend or family member to help you can always call us

title: Are You Cyclone Ready?
text: here at Embrace. What’s Your Plan? Now is the time to have a plan ready. If this is your first cyclone, part of being prepared might be to do some extra research on what to expect during a cyclone. A great resource is this page which has photos and info about what may happen. Think about your unique circumstances. If you live in a free-standing house, you’ll need to bring in furniture and anything else that could fly about: these items can smash into windows or roofs. Ask a friend or neighbour to assist you if need be. If you’re in an apartment you’ll still need to tape down your windows and have water ready. Again, a neighbour might be happy to help if you need it. If you live with pets you’ll need to arrange food and water for them, or get someone to do it for you. If you are living alone now is the time to check in with family and friends and discuss your cyclone plan with them. If you need medical equipment, get it ready and have a stock of supplies in case the shops are closed for a while. You don’t need to be alone: ask a neighbour, friend or family member to stay with you during the cyclone. And as soon as it’s safe to do so, Embrace carers can visit and assess your needs. We’re here to help!

title: Community Nursing: Quality care where you need it most.
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: NDIS , Western Australia , Community Nursing , Pilbara , Embrace , Karratha Community Nursing: Quality care where you need it most. Let’s be honest—hospitals are great when you need them, but nobody dreams of spending more time there than absolutely necessary. That’s where community nursing steps in! It brings top-notch healthcare straight to where you feel most comfortable—your home, local clinic, or residential care home. At Embrace Healthcare Solutions , we provide NDIS-funded community nursing services to individuals with disabilities, ensuring they receive the care they need without the stress of hospital visits. Whether it’s managing long-term conditions, assisting with personal care, or helping with recovery after a hospital stay, community nursing empowers people to live healthier, more independent lives. Why Community Nursing is a game-changer for people with disabilities 1. Hospital-level care without the hospital feel Imagine getting professional medical care in your own home, without the beeping machines and sterile smells of a hospital. Sounds great, right? Community nurses are highly trained professionals who assess individual needs and provide tailored support—whether it’s wound care, chronic condition management, or everyday personal assistance. Plus, having a dedicated nurse check in on you regularly means better communication between you and your medical team, reducing unnecessary hospital visits. 2. Holistic Care – More than just bandages and check-ups Community nurses don’t just tick off a checklist and leave rather they take a holistic

title: Community Nursing: Quality care where you need it most.
text: approach, addressing both medical and personal needs. They assist with: ✅ Medication management (so you never miss a dose!) ✅ Wound care and treatment plans ✅ Personal care assistance ✅ Respiratory and stoma management ✅ Overnight nursing support The best part? Everything is tailored to you. Whether you need moderate, intensive, or primary care, community nurses adapt to what works best for your lifestyle. 3. Smoother recovery after a hospital stay Hospitals are great for treatment, but getting back to normal life can be tricky—especially if you have complex care needs. That’s where community nursing steps in. If you’ve just had surgery or a hospital stay, community nurses help ease the transition by: ✅ Developing treatment plans in coordination with doctors ✅ Monitoring progress and spotting any issues early ✅ Providing ongoing support to speed up recovery For those with long-term conditions, community nurses fill the gap between hospital care and daily life, ensuring consistent, high-quality support. 4. It’s all about independence Let’s get one thing straight—community nursing isn’t just about helping you get better; it’s about helping you live better. Nurses focus on empowering individuals to be as self-sufficient as possible. Whether that means: 💡 Teaching self-care techniques 💡 Encouraging mobility and rehabilitation 💡 Adjusting care plans to promote independence The goal? To equip you with the tools, confidence, and support to live life your way. 5. Saving money while staying healthy Did you know community nursing helps cut down healthcare costs? By providing preventative care, nurses reduce the

title: Community Nursing: Quality care where you need it most.
text: risk of hospital admissions and expensive treatments. They also: 💰 Educate patients on managing their conditions 💰 Help prevent complications 💰 Provide at-home treatments that keep costs down For families, this means less financial strain and more peace of mind knowing that loved ones are well cared for. 6. Trust and personalised support Wouldn’t it be great if your nurse knew you personally, rather than treating you like just another appointment? With community nursing, trust and familiarity are built over time. Regular visits mean nurses understand your preferences, routines, and concerns, making care more personalised and effective. And let’s be real – when you feel comfortable with your healthcare provider, you’re more likely to speak up about what you need, leading to better outcomes. Final Thoughts: the heart of community healthcare At Embrace Healthcare Solutions , we believe quality healthcare should fit around your life—not the other way around. Community nursing allows people with disabilities to receive top-tier medical support without compromising their independence. From personal care to complex medical needs, our nurses provide compassionate, professional, and tailored support to help you or your loved ones live life to the fullest. Want to learn more about how community nursing could help you? Visit our website or give us a call—we’d love to chat!

title: Conversations that count: Embrace at St Luke’s Careers Day
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: NDIS , Inclusivity , Employment , Careers Conversations that count: Embrace at St Luke’s Careers Day In June, the team from Embrace Healthcare Solutions had the pleasure of attending the Year 10 Speed Careering Conversations at St Luke’s College in Karratha. It was a lively and inspiring event that brought together over 25 employers from across the Pilbara, offering students a meaningful opportunity to explore future career paths in a supportive and engaging setting. The event was designed to help students consider the five career pathways offered at St Luke’s College. From the moment it began, the room was filled with energy as students eagerly moved between tables, engaging with professionals from a wide range of industries including mining, corporate services, trades, health, and community care. Representing the care sector, our team from Embrace was delighted to see such a strong interest in what we do. Many students admitted they had not thought much about careers in healthcare or disability support before, but that quickly changed once the conversations started. We brought along our “Care to Guess?” quiz and a few small gifts, which turned out to be a real hit. Teachers even told us that our table was the most colourful and the most engaged on the day. As students stepped up to our table, they asked insightful questions about the roles available in our field. They were curious about support

title: Conversations that count: Embrace at St Luke’s Careers Day
text: work, administration, and how we assess someone’s level of disability. Several students wanted to understand how the NDIS works, what qualifications are needed, and what a typical day might look like for someone in a caring profession. It was a pleasure to be able to break down some of those big ideas into conversations that made sense to young people who are just beginning to explore their future. There was a genuine sense of curiosity, and in some cases, a spark of inspiration. We could see students starting to imagine themselves in roles that are centred on helping others and making a real difference in their communities. We are grateful to the staff and organisers at St Luke’s College for inviting us to be part of such a valuable initiative. Events like these are more than just career expos. They are spaces where students can ask questions, connect with professionals, and discover possibilities they may not have considered before. At Embrace, we believe that care is not just a career, it is a contribution. And it was a privilege to share that message with the students of Karratha. Credits: St Luke’s College Karratha for granting us permission to use the cover image.

title: Embracing Aged Care: A new chapter for our community.
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: HCP , Trilogy , Aged Care Embracing Aged Care: A new chapter for our community. Recently, Embrace Healthcare Solutions had the privilege of participating in the Aged Care Workforce Strategy Summit in Karratha , jointly hosted by Regional Development Australia and Ageing Australia. It was more than a professional event. It became a meaningful opportunity to reflect, to connect, and to share where we are heading, that is, towards a future where aged care is compassionate, community led, and grounded in trust. The summit unfolded over two thoughtful and purpose filled days. On the first day, we gathered with sector leaders, frontline workers, policymakers, and educators to explore some of the most pressing challenges in aged care. Together, we discussed how to strengthen recruitment, improve retention, support training, and protect the wellbeing of staff. These were not just formal discussions, but honest conversations shaped by lived experience and shared purpose. The second day centred around the people who matter most, our elders . We were honoured to take part in the Seniors Afternoon Tea and Information Session, themed “Your Care, Your Community.” This session featured talks on accessing local health services, allied health, home support, and advanced care planning through ELDAC. But beyond the information shared, it was the personal connections that truly stood out. We spoke directly with seniors from across the region, listened to their hopes, and answered their thoughtful

title: Embracing Aged Care: A new chapter for our community.
text: questions. During the afternoon, Embrace announced our new partnership with Trilogy Care. From 1 July 2025, we began offering services under the Aged Care Support at Home funding. We also shared our intention to expand into Commonwealth Home Support Programme delivery within the next twelve months. The response from the community was warm and encouraging. Many were already familiar with our work under the Palliative Care funding through WACHS Pilbara, and welcomed the news of our continued presence in aged care. One of the lighter moments came from Liz Behjat, Western Australia and Northern Territory Manager at Ageing Australia , who opened the summit with a smile and a comment about wanting an Embrace shirt to match her hair colour. At the end of the event, we gifted her one. It was a simple gesture, but one that captured the spirit of the summit: friendly, generous, and people focused . Since our aged care services commenced on 1 July, we have experienced a significant rise in enquiries. This has reaffirmed what we have long known that people in the Pilbara want aged care that is personal, accessible, and delivered with integrity. We are also an official member of Ageing Australia and this marks another step in our commitment to listening, learning, and growing in partnership with others who care deeply about this work. At Embrace, we believe aged care is not simply a service, it is a relationship. It is about showing up, staying present, and walking alongside those who

title: Embracing Aged Care: A new chapter for our community.
text: have spent their lives giving to others. It is our privilege to now care for them. And in Karratha, this is only the beginning .

title: From learning to earning: The transformational impact of the Health Sector Work Ready Program
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: Ashburton Aboriginal Corporation , NDIS , Pilbara , Embrace , Community participation From learning to earning: The transformational impact of the Health Sector Work Ready Program The journey from learning to earning is no small feat, but for the participants of the Health Sector Work Ready Program, it has been a rewarding adventure filled with growth, discovery, and newfound purpose. Run in collaboration with the Ashburton Aboriginal Corporation (AAC), the program aims to build a culturally sensitive and people-centred healthcare workforce in the Pilbara. Embrace Healthcare Solutions had the privilege of hosting several participants. Over the past few weeks, they have moved beyond the classroom to apply their skills in real-world healthcare settings, gaining hands-on experience and boosting their employability. Empowering skills & confidence For many participants, entering the healthcare sector required them to overcome personal barriers. Some came in unsure of their abilities or uncertain about the path ahead. But through a blend of structured training, work placements, and the encouragement of mentors, they have discovered confidence they didn’t know they had. Each participant was given the opportunity to practice their skills in a supportive and guided environment, building a solid foundation for their future careers. From mastering personal care routines to understanding complex medical processes, these participants are now better prepared to face the challenges of healthcare roles with confidence and capability. Real-world experience with real-world impact While learning in

title: From learning to earning: The transformational impact of the Health Sector Work Ready Program
text: a classroom is essential, nothing beats real-world experience. That’s why the Work Ready Program provides placements with healthcare providers like Embrace Healthcare Solutions. By working alongside seasoned professionals, participants have gained firsthand experience with clients, learning the intricacies of care delivery. They have had the chance to see the human side of healthcare, building empathy and emotional intelligence that textbooks simply can’t teach. These experiences have offered them a taste of what a career in healthcare truly looks like — the triumphs, the challenges, and the profound satisfaction of making a difference in someone’s life. Mentorship and growth A key highlight of the program has been the mentorship and support participants received from both program facilitators and industry professionals. These connections have given jobseekers a clear view of potential career pathways, showing them that the healthcare sector offers not just jobs, but meaningful careers. For many, this mentorship has been the catalyst for their personal and professional growth, with some now seeking to pursue further training and upskilling opportunities in healthcare. By fostering a sense of belonging and purpose, the program is building a generation of healthcare workers with not only the skills to succeed but also the heart to care. Success stories: From jobseekers to hired professionals We are thrilled to announce that one of the participants, Kerry, has secured a position with us after completing the program. Her journey from learner to employed professional is a testament to the power of opportunity and support. Similarly, Linda, another participant,

title: From learning to earning: The transformational impact of the Health Sector Work Ready Program
text: has successfully secured a role with Western Diagnostic Pathology. These inspiring success stories demonstrate how a well-structured program, combined with hands-on experience and mentorship, can transform lives. Participants who once doubted their abilities now wear the badge of healthcare professionals with pride. Some are already supporting clients in the Pilbara community — a region we proudly call home. Next steps for participants For a few participants, like Damika, the program has sparked a deeper curiosity about the healthcare sector. While she initially joined to “test the waters,” Damika is now exploring opportunities for further training and development in the field. Others, like Kerry, have been inspired by the impact they can have on their local community. Kerry’s words ring true for many: “Embrace Health is the long-lost family I have been waiting for.” Her experience underscores the idea that working in healthcare is not just about employment — it’s about belonging, connection, and making a difference. Looking ahead The Health Sector Work Ready Program is more than just an initiative, it’s a transformative experience that changes lives and strengthens the healthcare workforce in the Pilbara. By equipping participants with the skills, knowledge, and real-world experience they need to succeed, this program is filling critical workforce gaps and supporting sustainable employment for Aboriginal community members. It’s a step forward for participants, a win for the community, and a testament to the power of collaboration. For more updates on this program and other initiatives at Embrace Healthcare Solutions, stay connected with us

title: Harmony in Care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: Employment , Western Australia , Pilbara , Harmony Day Harmony in Care Harmony Week is especially meaningful for organisations like Embrace, because cultural diversity is not an abstract idea in care, it is actually lived every day through the people who show up to support children, older Australians, and people living with disability. In Australia, the care and support workforce is one of the country’s largest and fastest growing workforces. Health Care and Social Assistance accounts for around 15 per cent of Australia’s workforce, and Census data shows that more than 40 per cent of Registered Nurses and Aged and Disabled Carers were born overseas. Almost 40,000 people working in those occupations had arrived in Australia since 2016, a share well above the national average across all occupations. That is one of the reasons Harmony Week matters so much. Officially, Harmony Week celebrates Australia’s cultural diversity and the values of inclusiveness, respect and belonging for everyone. In 2026, it runs from 16 to 22 March and includes 21 March, which is also the United Nations International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination. At Embrace, Harmony Week is also a chance to recognise the real people behind Australia’s growing care economy. This year, we are proud to celebrate one of our own: David Appiah . David migrated from Ghana to build a life in Australia, not only for himself and his family,

title: Harmony in Care
text: but also in service of the community he and his wife now call home. At Embrace, David has become a valued support worker whose care, presence and commitment reflect the very heart of what this sector is about. His wife, Anastasia, is also part of the care economy, working in child care. Together, they represent something deeply important about modern Australia: families who arrive with hope, work hard, care for others, and help strengthen the communities around them. With the support of Embrace, David has been able to continue building a life for himself and his family, including their three beautiful daughters. His story is one of contribution, resilience and belonging. It is also a reminder that when we welcome people into our communities and workplaces, we do not just fill jobs but we build stronger neighbourhoods, richer cultures, and a more compassionate country. This Harmony Week, we celebrate David, Anastasia, and all the care workers from around the world who are helping shape Australia’s future through kindness, service and dedication. We thank them for the care they give so generously, and for the many ways they help our communities thrive. At Embrace, we believe harmony is more than a theme for one week of the year. It is something we live through respect, shared purpose, and care for one another. And in a world that can sometimes feel divided, we also take this moment to wish for something bigger: global harmony, peace, and a deeper sense of humanity for

title: Harmony in Care
text: all.

title: More opportunities for employment announced
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: NDIS , Inclusivity , Employment , Embrace More opportunities for employment announced There’s some exciting news for people living with a disability who might be looking for work: not only has the government renewed its pledge to fully fund the NDIS, which is reassuring, but there has been some new additions to the Disability Employment Program, which will soon be re-named Inclusive Employment Australia, and more people will be able to access it. New changes coming into effect The new program will expand the criteria for eligibility, to include: 1. People who have an assessed future work capacity of less than 8 hours per week, and; 2. People who do not receive an income support payment. This is an inclusive strategy to support more people to get into work. It’s welcome news for industries such as hospitality, where new staff is in high demand since the pandemic. According to a national report released by All Things Equal, over a thousand jobs can be earmarked for people living with a disability, to help get hospitality back on track. The government agrees, too, as they have pledged more money to the wage subsidies program– up to $10,000 per person– so there’s a decent incentive for employers to consider a person living with a disability to be a part of their team. So it’s not just up to job-seekers to convince employers to give them

title: More opportunities for employment announced
text: a fair go: this incentive is helping to convince employers that a person with a disability can be a great choice for their organisation. What’s also helpful is that the two-year service limit will be removed, so if you need more time to study or build your skills to find employment, you’ll be better supported. If you’re already a participant in the current Disability Employment Program, you aren’t required to do anything. All benefits will remain the same, and you’re encouraged to continue to work with your provider. These new changes will come into effect on July 1st, 2025, and although there is limited information about the new program for now, it does bring hope that there is a renewed interest in supporting people with a disability to find employment and have a fair go. If you would like to be on our mailing list to learn more about this new program, DM us on fb. When we know more about the new program we’ll let you know.

title: Pilbara’s healthcare hop-on hop-off: building a skilled workforce
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: Ashburton Aboriginal Corporation , NDIS , Pilbara , Embrace Pilbara’s healthcare hop-on hop-off: building a skilled workforce Over the last few weeks, we’ve had the privilege of hosting participants from the Health Sector Work Ready Program, offered by Ashburton Aboriginal Corporation. This initiative is designed to create a skilled workforce capable of delivering culturally sensitive, people-centred care. As part of the program, participants ‘hop on and hop off’ with various care providers across the Pilbara region, gaining diverse skill sets and valuable experiences. Among those who ‘hopped on’ at Embrace Healthcare are two inspiring individuals, Damika and Kerry, who have spent the past two weeks learning alongside our dedicated care team. Damika, a vibrant 24-year-old from Karratha, joined the program out of curiosity and a desire to explore a potential career in healthcare. Drawn to helping others, particularly those with disability needs, she saw this as an opportunity to gain valuable insights into care delivery. While she’s still deciding whether to pursue a long-term career in the sector, her time at Embrace Healthcare has been eye-opening. Working closely with experienced professionals, Damika has developed a deeper appreciation for the impact that compassionate care can have on individuals and their families. Whatever path she chooses, Damika now has a solid foundation to guide her journey. Kerry, a compassionate 47-year-old, has embraced the relaxed yet purposeful environment of Embrace’s workshops. Inspired by the care

title: Pilbara’s healthcare hop-on hop-off: building a skilled workforce
text: her aunt receives from Embrace, Kerry joined the program to make a meaningful difference in her community. Many of the clients she supports are part of her extended friends and family network, which makes her work all the more personal and fulfilling. title: The Money Series – Getting Creative (Part-1)
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: NDIS , Western Australia , Pilbara , Embrace , Karratha , cost of living crisis The Money Series – Getting Creative (Part-1) As the cost of living continues to rise in 2025, people with disabilities—especially in remote areas—are feeling the financial pressure more than ever. While recent government reports addressed general support, they overlooked additional measures for those living with disabilities. So it’s becoming even more necessary for Australians living with a disability, to keep looking for ways to save money. Welcome to our Money Series! For our first week, we’re starting out with something fun: saving or earning money by being creative. There might be something that you can do that others would pay money for, even if it’s a small price for a small thing. Your set of skills, experiences and knowledge are completely unique to you, and you may be exactly what others are looking for. You could charge money for your goods or services, or you could choose to barter. There are plenty of Buy, Swap and Sell groups on Facebook that offer both options, and it’s worth spending some time here. And if you have a business idea you’d like to explore, consider applying for a grant with the City of Karratha council. So we are sharing our top five tips to save or make a little bit of extra money while getting creative, and we’d love

title: The Money Series – Getting Creative (Part-1)
text: to hear your ideas too: make a comment on our Facebook page and we’ll give it some love in return! 1. Cook It Are you a whizz in the kitchen? Can you whip up a batch of yummy, nutritious meals and whack in a dessert or yummy snack for good measure? Because there are plenty of time-poor people who are ready to pay for a home-cooked meal. Think mothers who have just given birth, elderly people, or families with both parents working full-time. You don’t need a commercial kitchen if you are only selling to family and friends, and are not selling “for profit” (check out what this means here). But if you’ve trialled this venture and love it, and you want to go into business, you could hire out a commercial kitchen on a casual basis and scale up your work. Just remember to keep honest with the ATO and with the Australian Business Register, and check with the council about food regulations. 2. Sew It Perhaps there’s an old sewing machine gathering dust at the back of a cupboard, and it could save money for you, or even earn it. If you already have sewing skills then now’s the time to put them to good use! You can pick up clothes cheaply at second hand shops, and if they don’t quite suit you, there are many ways to make it your own, for example buying a pair of denim trousers and cutting off some length and hemming them

title: The Money Series – Getting Creative (Part-1)
text: to make shorts. People will pay for their trousers to be hemmed too, or other small fixes to a garment. And then there’s sewing from scratch: maybe there is an item that can’t be found easily in the shops, such as a bowl cozy, a library bag or even a child’s bomber jacket… and selling online is an easy way to start finding customers. Again, you can source cheap fabric from second hand shops. Old doona covers, anyone? Just remember the same rules apply for selling as a hobby as opposed to a business, and if you need more info just look here. 3. Mr FixIt Or Mrs FixIt. If you love to get on the tools, this one is for you. We’re thinking on a small scale here: repairing a coffee table leg, servicing a sewing machine, re-carpeting a cat’s scratching pole, repairing a children’s toy, etc. Some people go on “scavenger hunts” at the Seven Mile Waste Facility and fix small appliances, furniture or toys, and sell them on. This would be considered a hobby under the ATO’s strict rules and could be a great little money spinner if you enjoy tinkering. Alternatively, you could barter your goods if you’re not interested in the hassle of selling. An important note: please only fix electrical appliances if you are qualified. There are plenty of other items to repair and sell/barter that don’t require a licence. 4. Grow It Calling all greenthumbs! As food costs keep rising, people are looking

title: The Money Series – Getting Creative (Part-1)
text: for cheaper ways to source their fresh fruit and veggies, and even though our area is considered a northern arid zone, so long as they have access to water, plenty of things can be planted all year round. A good guide to start with can be found here. Even if you don’t choose to sell your produce, they’ll be delicious to eat yourself, and there may be interesting varieties of fruit and veg that aren’t in the shops. Or perhaps you know of a few households who need to keep their weeds down, or have their veggies sprayed with your secret blend of insect repellant, or even just have their plants watered regularly. Kids can earn pocket money for simple garden chores like these, too. If you have chooks (and they’re laying), now is the time to consider selling or bartering those eggs: there are currently egg shortages in supermarkets due to the avian flu issues from last year, and until supplies are high again, there will be plenty of customers looking to buy at markets, on the roadside, or even through Marketplace. 5. Teach It What is your most valuable asset? Your mind. There are so many things you can teach someone else, and your knowledge can be valuable. You may wish to charge a fee for your services, or maybe you’d feel more comfortable bartering, for example, giving homework help to your neighbour’s school-aged child in exchange for a home-cooked meal, a lift to the shops, your mail

title: The Money Series – Getting Creative (Part-1)
text: to be collected for you, your bins brought out and in each week, your lawn to have the sprinkler put over it, odd jobs to be done around the house… the possibilities are endless! You could also: Coach a sport you know and love; Or if you can no longer play, coach tactics for that sport; Listen to children read, and read books to them; Tutor an adult student in a particular software application (maybe you know Photoshop, or you’re a spreadsheet ninja?); Give local gardening advice; Hold small group lessons for sewing, cooking, makeup, art, vehicle mechanics, an instrument, or dance. Coach a sport you know and love; Or if you can no longer play, coach tactics for that sport; Listen to children read, and read books to them; Tutor an adult student in a particular software application (maybe you know Photoshop, or you’re a spreadsheet ninja?); Give local gardening advice; Hold small group lessons for sewing, cooking, makeup, art, vehicle mechanics, an instrument, or dance. But really, it’s all about community… …especially in remote areas where people rely on each other. By sharing skills, services, and support, we can create stronger connections and financial security. Don’t be afraid to reach out to a neighbour, club, or local community group. Your unique skills could make a difference, and you might even save or make some money too. Leave a comment on your best tip for being creative: we can’t wait to read it! A word about our words: We

title: The Money Series – Getting Creative (Part-1)
text: are not financial planners, nor are we associated with any financial institutions. Our advice is purely for thought-provoking purposes only, and if you have concerns or questions about your financial situation please speak with a financial planner or a Centrelink representative. If you are interested in starting a business, please visit the ATO’s website or use this link as a starter. Earning money for the purposes of a business will attract tax and other responsibilities, so please make sure you’re staying within the bounds of Australian business and tax laws before embarking on any business-like endeavours. title: The Money Series – Transport (Part 2)
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Published by: Sam | Category: NDIS , Western Australia , Transport , Pilbara , Embrace , Karratha The Money Series – Transport (Part 2) As petrol prices keep rising, it’s more expensive than ever to get around. Maybe you need a lift to the shops and back, or perhaps you have appointments to get to. And many of us need to ride long distances to access services. The Pilbarra is huge and the kilometres can really add up, which can be a burden on finances. So welcome to our second installment of our Money Series, where we take a close look at ways you can save money and still enjoy life during this worldwide financial crisis. Whether you’re a patient who needs a long ride to get to specialist treatment, or a person who requires extra mobility support, check out our top tips for getting from A to B for less. NDIS Transport Funding: When there’s no option to use public transport, or if a participant is unable to travel independently, NDIS participants may be eligible for transport funding. This includes private cars, taxis and ridesharing. To check if you are eligible visit here . Patient Assisted Travel Scheme (PATS): For residents needing to travel long distances for specialist medical services not available locally, PATS provides financial subsidies to offset travel and accommodation costs. For more info, see here . Companion Card WA: The Companion Card Program

title: The Money Series – Transport (Part 2)
text: supports Western Australians with a significant and permanent disability who require attendant care support to participate at community venues and events. Companion Cardholders show their card when booking or purchasing a ticket from a participating business, called an Affiliate. Affiliates will recognise the Companion Card and issue the cardholder with a second ticket for their companion at no charge. Check if you’re eligible here . TransWA Concession Fares: If you’re a concession card holder, you are entitled to concession fares and limited free travel on Transwa services. To know more, see here . Passenger Transport Subsidy Scheme (PTSS): The PTSS is a subsidy available to eligible people with disability travelling in on-demand rank or hail (taxi) vehicles. PTSS participants can receive up to 75% off eligible taxi fares. The PTSS replaces the TUSS (Taxi User Subsidy Scheme). To see if you’re eligible click here . Regional Pensioner Travel Card: The Travel Card supports eligible country pensioners with travel costs to access government services to enhance their quality of life. This card provides eligible pensioners with up to $675 a year towards the cost of fuel and/or taxi travel from participating providers, offering more support for the transport needs of pensioners living in regional areas. For more information, see here . Carpooling: And lastly, why not hop in for a ride with others, and you can all keep the costs down? There are ridesharing apps available, or simply use social media such as a Facebook local group to organise a trip

title: The Money Series – Transport (Part 2)
text: together. And the best part about this is that you can get to know new people while cutting down on petrol money. Have a tip you’d like to share? We’d love to hear it! Leave a comment on our fb page and we’ll look into it straight away.

text: Harmony in Care Harmony Week is especially meaningful for organisations like Embrace, because cultural diversity is not an abstract idea in care, it is actually lived every day through the people who show up to support children, older Australians, and people living with disability. In Australia, the care and support workforce is one of the country’s largest and fastest growing workforces. Health Care and Social Assistance accounts for around 15 per cent of Australia’s workforce, and Census data shows that more than 40 per cent of Registered Nurses and Aged and Disabled Carers were born overseas. Almost 40,000 people working in those occupations had arrived in Australia since 2016, a share well above the national average across all occupations. That is one of the reasons Harmony Week matters so much. Officially, Harmony Week celebrates Australia’s cultural diversity and the values of inclusiveness, respect and belonging for everyone. In 2026, it runs from 16 to 22 March and includes 21 March, which is also the United Nations International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination. At Embrace, Harmony Week is also a chance to recognise the real people behind Australia’s growing care economy. This year, we are proud to celebrate one of our own: David Appiah . David migrated from Ghana to build a life in Australia, not only for himself and his family, but also in service of the community he and his wife now call home. At Embrace, David has become a valued support worker whose care, presence and

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: commitment reflect the very heart of what this sector is about. His wife, Anastasia, is also part of the care economy, working in child care. Together, they represent something deeply important about modern Australia: families who arrive with hope, work hard, care for others, and help strengthen the communities around them. With the support of Embrace, David has been able to continue building a life for himself and his family, including their three beautiful daughters. His story is one of contribution, resilience and belonging. It is also a reminder that when we welcome people into our communities and workplaces, we do not just fill jobs but we build stronger neighbourhoods, richer cultures, and a more compassionate country. This Harmony Week, we celebrate David, Anastasia, and all the care workers from around the world who are helping shape Australia’s future through kindness, service and dedication. We thank them for the care they give so generously, and for the many ways they help our communities thrive. At Embrace, we believe harmony is more than a theme for one week of the year. It is something we live through respect, shared purpose, and care for one another. And in a world that can sometimes feel divided, we also take this moment to wish for something bigger: global harmony, peace, and a deeper sense of humanity for all. Read More

Embrace collects dirty laundry or linen from the participant’s house, launders them at Embrace facilities, and returns the cleaned laundry to the participant’s house. This support is essential for maintaining hygiene and comfort for our participants. Preparation and Delivery of Meals This service helps with the costs of preparing and delivering meals to participants who can’t manage this themselves, if they don’t already receive similar support. It’s important to note that while the service covers preparation and delivery costs, the cost of the food itself is not included in the NDIS funding. Meals are prepared at Embrace Facilities and delivered to our client’s home. This ensures participants have access to ready-to-eat meals, enhancing their daily living quality.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Community engagement Participate in fulfilling activities within your community. We’re committed to offering creative and individualised assistance, empowering participants to achieve their aspirations, forge relationships, and enhance self-reliance. Our services include Social engagement & community involvement Life brightens up when you’re out and about, sharing moments with others. If you need support to make this happen, we’re here for you. Whether it’s navigating public transport, joining a social club, enrolling in a course, or attending events – we’ve got you covered. We’re here to help you forge new friendships, broaden your social circle, and boost your confidence in social settings. At Embrace, we ensure you to truly relish being part of your community. High intensity support This support service by Embrace, ensures that participants needing High Intensity Supports can fully engage in community, social, and recreational activities, with the help of skilled and experienced support workers. It’s also applicable when participants require aid from disability support workers and registered nurses with specific high intensity support skills outlined in the NDIS Practice Standards. At Embrace, we will take care of our clients, irrespective of their disability or medical condition.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Community nursing We strive always to ensure that no matter what type of attention may be needed, our highly experienced staff are ready to deliver excellent care every step along the way. Our team of expert nurses and caregivers provide personalised plans, programs, and supports that empower caregivers to confidently care for you or your loved ones. Our Community Nursing includes services ranging from helping with appointments to complex tasks or care. Our community nursing plan includes Bowel care Our service includes assisting with personal hygiene while maintaining strict cleanliness and safety standards. We acknowledge the private nature of our support and always seek your consent before proceeding. Our carers monitor health indicators, such as changes in bowel movements, and administer treatments like laxatives safely, consulting a healthcare professional when necessary. For more complex needs, we manage non-routine medication, ensuring you receive comprehensive support tailored to your requirements. Enteral Feeding Management We maintain hygiene, manage enteral feeding with consent, and monitor for safety. We keep the stoma clean, address equipment issues, and adjust feeding as needed. Collaborating with healthcare professionals, we respond to health changes, ensuring proper nutrition and intervention. High-risk tasks, like Nasogastric (NG) tube replacement, are healthcare practitioner duties, though we can assist with PEG tube issues under medical supervision. Diabetes Monitoring Support for diabetes management involves aiding individuals who require assistance with implementing their diabetes care plan, including but not limited to (particularly) those

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: needing help with regular diabetes monitoring and (insulin) management. This support encompasses understanding diabetes, symptom prevention, control and management. Collaborating with individuals to implement their management plans effectively, ensuring their health and wellbeing. Severe Dysphagia Management Our service focuses on supporting individuals with difficulty swallowing (dysphagia). We identify those in need and refer them to specialists for assessment. We’re trained to manage meal plans and ensure meals are safe and enjoyable, with the right food texture and proper oral hygiene. Communication about meal preferences is key, as is promoting independence during mealtimes. We closely monitor and respond to any eating or drinking issues to ensure safety and enjoyment of meals. Urinary Catheter Management Our care includes managing catheter care for individuals with indwelling and suprapubic catheters, encompassing the replacement and disposal of bags and health monitoring. While health practitioners handle catheter insertion, support workers may manage catheters under strict professional oversight, ensuring high-intensity support and safety. This care is crucial for the comfort and health of those we support, providing peace of mind and maintaining hygiene. Complex Wound Management Our service includes assisting individuals who need help with any wound care including but not limited to pressure care and managing wounds. Normally, a qualified nurse would handle wound care, but our trained support workers can provide basic care under the guidance of healthcare professionals. They’re trained for these tasks, ensuring safe and effective care according to wound care specialist care plan. (without needing specialist skills.) This support is essential for

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: maintaining health and comfort. Stoma Care Our care includes support for individuals with stomas, like colostomy and ileostomy, or tracheostomy care that doesn’t involve ventilation. Our team is knowledgeable in the basics of the eliminatory system, caring for the skin and stoma, using equipment properly, and safe positioning and monitoring techniques. We’re trained to recognise common risks and know when to call specialist healthcare professional for issues or malfunctions. This ensures safe, effective care for those we support. Medication Administration & Management Managing medication involves ensuring timely intake, keeping track of prescriptions, and monitoring for side effects. The carer assists with organising medications, understanding dosage instructions, and liaising with healthcare providers as needed. On-call overnight monitoring This service provides for overnight on-call assistance (either onsite or off-site) with, or supervision of, personal tasks of daily living. It applies to any day of the week and on public holidays. This support item is for an eight-hour period and includes up to one hour of active support provided to the participant for the duration of the period.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Group social activities At Embrace, we’re dedicated to aiding your involvement in the community and embracing its many advantages. Our Group Social and Community Participation Services are tailored to assist you in reaching your objectives, whether it’s joining clubs, attending events or acquiring new skills. We firmly believe in everyone’s right to contribute to their community actively, and we’re here to ensure you can seize that opportunity. Our services include Activities in a group setting These support services help participants engage in community, social, and recreational activities within a group environment, whether in a community setting or at a designated centre. This includes opportunities to join group outings, workshops, fitness classes, and cultural events. Our aim is to facilitate social interaction, build connections, and enhance overall well-being through shared experiences. High intensity activities These support services help participants needing High Intensity Supports to join community activities with others, whether it’s in local centres or out and about. We ensure they get the right assistance, especially when a highly skilled support worker or a registered nurse is needed. High intensity support involves regular assistance, at least once per shift, for managing challenging behaviours requiring intensive positive behaviour support.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… ILO package Individualised Living Options (ILOs) are personalised support packages developed by thoroughly considering each person’s likes, abilities, needs, and available support within their community and informal networks. An ILO focuses on the support provided rather than the housing itself and is independent of whether someone owns their home, rents, or is eligible for Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA) funding. This approach ensures tailored support that respects individual choices and circumstances. ILO providers are key in shaping a life vision through tailored support arrangements, aiding decisions on living situations and the enabling supports for a fulfilling life. An ILO is divided into two stages: Stage 1 – Exploration and Design , focusing on personalised planning and Stage 2 – Support Model, implementing the designed support framework. This structured approach ensures support aligns with individual preferences and life goals, facilitating meaningful living arrangements and comprehensive assistance. ILO Stages Available Stage 1 - Exploration and Design This support helps participants explore and design their Individualised Living Options (ILO). Providers assist in understanding the participant’s vision for their future home, explore strengths, and how various supports can enhance their life. They also help in choosing living arrangements and support structures, assess risks, and consider alternative options. The process involves designing a tailored support package with the participant, potentially including finding housing and connecting with other services. Stage 2 - Support Model The Individualised Living Option (ILO) is a tailored support package

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: that helps participants achieve their living goals. It combines primary and additional supports, using both formal services and help from family or friends. This flexible package also includes monitoring and redesigning resources to ensure it meets changing needs, all through collaboration between the participant, their family, or a chosen provider. At Embrace, we guide you in settling into your chosen home and conduct regular check-ins to ensure everything meets your needs. If adjustments are necessary, we’re here to assist with those too. Our role is to continuously monitor and support you, ensuring your living arrangement is always suited to your preferences and requirements.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Live-in carer This service provides for a person who either lives in the house of the participant or travels with the participant. The service provides assistance with, and/or supervision of, personal tasks of daily life to develop skills of the participant to live as autonomously as possible. Our services include Personal Care The carer assists with bathing, dressing, and grooming, promoting the participant’s hygiene and self-esteem. This includes skin care, oral hygiene, and hair care, tailored to individual abilities and preferences. Personal care is crucial for maintaining good health and a positive self-image. Meal Preparation The carer prepares balanced, nutritious meals, catering to specific dietary needs and preferences. This includes planning meals, cooking, and aiding with eating if necessary. The focus is on ensuring participants enjoy healthy, tasty meals that meet their dietary requirements. Grocery Shopping The carer assists with grocery shopping, selecting items that align with the participant’s dietary needs and personal preferences. This involves planning meals, managing budgets, and ensuring a steady supply of necessary groceries and household items. Medication Management Managing medication involves ensuring timely intake, keeping track of prescriptions, and monitoring for side effects. The carer assists with organising medications, understanding dosage instructions, and liaising with healthcare providers as needed. Housekeeping Light housekeeping duties include cleaning, doing laundry, and maintaining an orderly environment. This ensures the participant’s living space is clean, safe, and comfortable, which is vital for their wellbeing and quality of

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: life. Companionship Offering companionship involves engaging in conversations, participating in hobbies or interests, and providing emotional support. This social interaction is vital for mental health, reducing feelings of isolation and loneliness. Mobility Assistance The carer assists with walking, transfers, and using mobility aids. This includes helping the participant move around their home safely and comfortably, and may involve exercises to maintain or improve mobility.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Maintaining employment Our team of Employment Development Officers will collaborate with you to pinpoint your career aspirations and deliver tailored training to assist you in achieving your objectives. Whether it’s acquiring new job skills like operating weighing machines or pallet jacks, obtaining a forklift license, or developing skills for transitioning to mainstream employment, we’ll support you every step of the way. Our services include Specialised Supported Employment These support service is designed for individuals who are currently employed but may require additional assistance to perform their job tasks independently or need regular guidance and encouragement to stay focused, communicate effectively, or manage their behaviours at work. Support can be provided either one-on-one or in a group setting, complementing the existing support from employers. These supports are tailored to meet individual needs and may include various interventions such as on-the-job assessments, personalised training, and ongoing supervision to ensure meaningful participation in the workplace. We also offer assistance with personal care, managing complex needs, and non-face-to-face activities directly related to maintaining employment.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Medium Term Accom Medium Term Accommodation (MTA) offers temporary funding for housing during transition, such as awaiting home modifications. It’s for those with a future home but needing a place until arrangements are finalised. This support, lasting up to 90 days, covers accommodation costs, but participants must handle their food and daily expenses. Care services are billed separately, ensuring support during important transitional periods without using the NDIS plan for living costs. Our MTA offers Furnished Living Spaces Our accommodations are usually fully furnished, providing all necessary amenities for a comfortable stay. This includes kitchen facilities, allowing guests to prepare their own meals and enjoy a homely atmosphere. Cost-Efficiency Our medium-term accommodation often comes at more affordable nightly rates than short-term stays, offering a cost-effective solution that blends the affordability of long-term leases with the flexibility of short-term rentals.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Mental health support The Capacity Building Category in your NDIS plan aims to boost your independence, skillset, and community involvement, tailoring activities to your needs and goals. It includes the Improved Relationships supports, offering strategies and interventions to enhance communication and behaviour, fostering a better social life and support network. Our mental health support plan provides Building Positive Behaviours: A Supportive Approach Our specialist behaviour intervention support focuses on intensive strategies to address and reduce harmful or persistent behaviours. By developing a personalised behaviour support plan, we aim to prevent such behaviours from emerging or worsening. This plan includes positive support strategies tailored for you, your family, and support network, striving for the best outcomes in reducing or eliminating concerns, fostering a supportive and understanding environment for growth and positive change. Unlocking Positive Paths Unlocking Positive Paths: Enhancing Communication and Behaviour dives into understanding each individual’s unique needs through assessments, spotlighting the importance of tailored support for daily engagement and improved social interactions. Addressing behaviours of concern with a positive plan helps navigate or eliminate challenges, ensuring a foundation built on understanding and collaboration with families and carers. This approach not only enriches relationships but also fosters a nurturing environment for personal growth and safety, transforming challenges into opportunities for development and enriching lives. Behaviour management The NDIS Improved Relationships funding helps create a behaviour support plan and provides training for caregivers and families to address and

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: reduce concerning behaviours linked to disabilities. This plan includes strategies to improve behaviour, enhance communication, and foster positive relationships, with training for those closely involved with the individual. It aims to identify what triggers challenging behaviours, offering solutions to manage or avoid these triggers, and works towards replacing difficult behaviours with positive ones, ensuring a supportive environment for everyone involved. Social Skills Development The NDIS Improved Relationships funding helps individuals enhance their social skills, focusing on better communication, active listening, empathy, conflict resolution, respect, and building relationships. It includes learning verbal and nonverbal cues, like body language and eye contact, and offers various learning formats such as individual, group, and online sessions. The support extends to participating in community, social, and recreational activities, alongside developing time management skills to boost independence and social engagement.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Personal domestic activities This service assists a participant to undertake or develop skills to maintain their home environment where the participant owns their own home or has sole or substantial responsibility for its maintenance. This Includes assisting participants to do basic house and yard work. Your domestic plan includes Gardening Support workers can assist NDIS participants with gardening tasks, creating an enjoyable and accessible outdoor space. This includes weeding, planting, and maintaining gardens, tailored to the participant’s preferences and capabilities. Gardening provides therapeutic benefits, promoting relaxation and a sense of achievement. Cleaning Cleaning support encompasses maintaining a clean and hygienic living environment. This involves tasks like dusting, vacuuming, and tidying, ensuring the participant’s home is comfortable and safe. Support workers adapt their cleaning methods to suit the specific needs and preferences of the participant. Meal Preparation Support workers aid in meal preparation, ensuring dietary needs and preferences are met. This includes planning, cooking, and possibly assisting with eating. Emphasis is placed on preparing nutritious meals that cater to the health requirements of the participant, fostering their independence and enjoyment of food.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Psychosocial Recovery Coaches Psychosocial Recovery Coaches guide individuals with psychosocial disabilities towards leading fuller lives by helping them access specific supports. They coach on recovery and decision-making, aiming for greater independence and crafting tailored Recovery and Crisis Management Plans. Leveraging their mental health expertise, our team ensures you receive top-notch support to achieve your goals. This plan includes Empowering Recovery and Building Resilience Our support focuses on nurturing strong, respectful relationships to empower individuals with psychosocial disabilities to lead fulfilling and contributory lives. Through the episodic journey of mental health, our Recovery Coaches maintain engagement, adapting to changing support needs. Working in harmony with participants, families, and carers, they craft and coordinate tailored NDIS supports. With both lived experience and professional qualifications, our coaches bring understanding and expertise to guide you towards resilience and independence.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Relationships support At Embrace, we offer specialised assessments for participants with complex or unclear needs. These assessments help determine the type of long-term or intensive support needed to address challenging behaviours. Our services include Behaviour Management Plan For participants experiencing challenges with their behaviour or social interactions, we provide a culturally safe tailored behaviour management plan to address their specific needs and enhance their quality of life. At Embrace, we focus on proactive strategies to prevent and appropriately manage challenging behaviour, including identifying triggers, fostering suitable learning environments, enhancing communication skills, establishing routines, and setting clear boundaries. Additionally, our plan incorporates reactive strategies to guide carers in responding to disruptive behaviour effectively, such as reminders, distractions, and trigger removal. Individual Social Skills Development At Embrace, our NDIS Improved Relationships service focuses on enhancing social skills for individuals. Our goal is to help them develop and practice effective communication and social interaction skills, fostering their participation in community activities. Through our support, individuals learn verbal and nonverbal communication techniques, including body language and eye contact. We also teach essential social skills like effective communication, active listening, empathy, conflict resolution, respect, and relationship building. Our services include individual and group learning opportunities, assistance in engaging in community activities, and learning time management skills. Activity Based Transport At Embrace, we offer Activity Based Transport services as part of our commitment to support community participation. This service provides transportation to and

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: from community activities, with our team also providing support at the destination. We also provide General Transport Services for activities not classified as support, such as trips to locations where services are provided by other providers or where no support is being delivered. Our aim is to ensure seamless transportation arrangements for our clients, facilitating their access to various activities and services.

We focus on enhancing confidence and comfort, ensuring each individual feels well-groomed and dignified. Our team is sensitive to the unique preferences of each participant, providing a respectful, empowering experience. We understand grooming’s role in personal wellbeing, and we’re committed to delivering a service that respects the independence and individuality of every NDIS participant. Cleaning Our cleaning service offers comprehensive, specialised cleaning to NDIS participants, creating a hygienic and orderly home environment. We tailor our services to individual preferences, recognising the unique needs of each participant. From regular housekeeping to deep cleaning, our skilled team ensures every corner is meticulously maintained. We focus on using eco-friendly products and methods to safeguard the health of our clients. Our commitment is to provide a clean, safe, and comfortable living space that enhances the wellbeing and independence of NDIS participants. Eating Eating assistance is crucial for many NDIS participants. Our service provides empathetic and skilled support for meal preparation and eating, tailored to the dietary needs and preferences of each individual. We assist in the entire process, from grocery shopping and cooking to feeding, ensuring meals are not only nutritious

Our staff are specially trained to offer support in a way that maintains dignity and respects personal boundaries. We focus on creating a relaxing environment, understanding that bathing is not just about hygiene but also a time for relaxation and rejuvenation. Our approach is to empower participants, assisting them as needed while encouraging self-sufficiency wherever possible. Dressing and undressing Dressing and undressing can be challenging for some NDIS participants. Our service offers respectful, personalised assistance in this daily task, ensuring comfort and promoting self-confidence. We assist with selecting appropriate attire, dressing, and undressing, all while respecting the individual’s choices and preferences. Our goal is to empower participants by providing support that fosters independence, helping them to start and end their day with dignity and ease. Toilet Toilet assistance is a sensitive aspect of daily care, and our service approaches it with the utmost respect for dignity and privacy. We offer discreet and compassionate support for toileting needs, focusing on hygiene and promoting independence. Our staff are trained to provide assistance in a way that respects the individual’s comfort and needs. We

We provide customised support to help individuals move safely and confidently within their homes and communities. Our approach includes assistance with walking, transfers, and using mobility aids. We aim to enhance the independence and quality of life for participants by enabling greater access to their environment and activities they enjoy. Our staff are trained in safe handling techniques and are committed to empowering participants through respectful, supportive mobility assistance.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Short Term Accom or Respite Care Our support includes short-term integrated care for self-care, accommodation, food, and activities at centres or group residences. Recognising the need for temporary comprehensive support, we offer Short Term Accommodation (STA) and respite services. These services provide a change from usual care arrangements, offering participants new support experiences while giving carers a well-deserved break. STA and respite aim to maintain ongoing care relationships by ensuring participants are well-supported during their carer’s absence. Our STA/Respite Plan includes Personal Care Personal care support focuses on assisting with daily routines such as bathing, dressing, and grooming. It’s not just about maintaining hygiene; it’s a brilliant opportunity to meet new people and make new friends. This service ensures individuals feel their best both physically and socially, enhancing their overall wellbeing. Accomodation Our accommodation provides a secure and comfortable living environment. It’s tailored to meet individual needs, ensuring everyone feels at home. This support prioritises safety, accessibility, and comfort, making it a cornerstone for a positive living experience. Food Our food service ensures access to nutritious and delicious meals tailored to individual dietary needs. It’s about more than just eating right; it’s about enjoying meals that contribute to overall health and wellbeing. This service guarantees that everyone enjoys balanced meals that fuel their day.

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Sleepover This service provides participant assistance with personal tasks of daily life where overnight support is needed, but the caregiver can sleep when not required to provide support. This support applies to any day of the week and on public holidays. Night-time Sleepover Supports must meet these conditions: The support begins before midnight to 06:00 the next day, lasting for a minimum continuous period of 8 hours. The support worker can sleep during times when their help is not required. Our overnight sleepover includes Meal Preparation Helping the participant prepare meals, ensuring they have a nutritious and enjoyable dinner. Bedtime Assistance Aiding the participant in getting ready for bed, which may include personal care routines. On-Call Support The support worker/ registered nurse remains ‘on call’ throughout the night. They can assist with tasks as needed, like toileting, managing medication, or responding to emergencies. Same as On-call overnight Monitoring

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: Scroll to top How can we help? Ask me anything about our services… Supported Independent Living (SIL) A group home, or shared home, provides a supportive environment for a small number of individuals requiring assistance, offering more personalised support compared to larger aged care facilities. It operates under the Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA) framework, focusing on the physical aspects of living arrangements, while Supported Independent Living (SIL) delivers personalised support for developing independence within this setting. Typically hosting up to three residents, group homes are designed for comfort, with support workers assisting in daily living tasks, ensuring an ideal balance of property suitability and care for NDIS participants. Your SIL plan includes Communal living Communal living focuses on teaching individuals how to coexist harmoniously with others and emphasises the importance of sharing household responsibilities. It’s about creating a supportive environment where everyone understands their duties, fostering a sense of community and mutual respect. This approach not only enhances daily living skills but also promotes interpersonal growth, making communal living an enriching experience for those involved. Household activities Assisting with household activities includes helping with essential tasks like meal preparation, cleaning, and gardening. This support is aimed at ensuring a well-maintained living space, promoting a healthy lifestyle through nutritious meals, and keeping the home environment clean and orderly. It’s about making daily chores manageable and fostering a sense of accomplishment and well-being. Everyday skills Everyday Skills encompasses essential life skills aimed at fostering independence and social integration. It includes managing finances,

title: Embrace – Embrace health care
text: ensuring individuals can budget and pay bills efficiently; developing social skills, crucial for building and maintaining positive relationships; and enhancing written communication, assisting with the understanding and completion of forms. These areas are vital for personal development, enabling individuals to navigate daily life confidently, manage their affairs effectively, and interact successfully with others in various social contexts.

This variety ensures we can cater to the unique requirements of each client, providing accessible and comfortable travel solutions for accessing disability supports and fulfilling personal goals. Our commitment is to ensure reliable, tailored transport services for every client’s convenience and independence. Our fleet options Our fleet At Embrace Healthcare Solutions, we warmly welcome our clients with a range of transportation options to meet every need. Our fleet includes both standard vehicles for ease of travel and specially equipped mobility vehicles, such as the Toyota Hiace, Toyota Voxy, and Toyota Alphard, designed for comfort and accessibility. All our vehicles are GPS tracked and are equipped with Driver Behaviour Monitoring System and Dash Cams to provide extra level of safety for our clients.
